docs.text: This document provides detailed information about the Integration API for the Open AXI Interconnect system. The Integration API enables seamless connection of the interconnect with external systems, processors, and peripherals.

docs.title: Top-Level Interface
docs.text:
The Open AXI Interconnect exposes a standard AXI4-Lite master interface for integration with external masters:

module axi_subsystem #(
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 32
)(
    input  logic                    clk,
    input  logic                    rst_n,

    // AXI4-Lite master interface
    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   awaddr,
    input  logic                    awvalid,
    output logic                    awready,

    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   wdata,
    input  logic [(DATA_WIDTH/8)-1:0] wstrb,
    input  logic                    wvalid,
    output logic                    wready,

    output logic [1:0]              bresp,
    output logic                    bvalid,
    input  logic                    bready,

    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   araddr,
    input  logic                    arvalid,
    output logic                    arready,

    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   rdata,
    output logic [1:0]              rresp,
    output logic                    rvalid,
    input  logic                    rready,

    // External peripheral signals
    output logic                    uart_tx,
    input  logic                    uart_rx,
    output logic                    timer_irq,
    inout  logic [31:0]             gpio_pins
);

docs.title: RAM Controller Driver
docs.text:
typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t control;
    volatile uint32_t status;
    volatile uint32_t address;
    volatile uint32_t data;
} ram_controller_t;

#define RAM_CONTROLLER ((ram_controller_t*) RAM_BASE)

void ram_init(void) {
    RAM_CONTROLLER->control = 0x1;  // Enable RAM
    while (!(RAM_CONTROLLER->status & 0x1));  // Wait for ready
}

docs.title: UART Driver
docs.text:
typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t ctrl;
    volatile uint32_t status;
    volatile uint32_t tx_data;
    volatile uint32_t rx_data;
} uart_controller_t;

#define UART_CONTROLLER ((uart_controller_t*) UART_BASE)

void uart_init(void) {
    UART_CONTROLLER->ctrl = 0x7;  // Enable UART, TX, RX
    while (!(UART_CONTROLLER->status & 0x1));  // Wait for TX ready
}

void uart_putc(char c) {
    while (!(UART_CONTROLLER->status & 0x1));  // Wait for TX ready
    UART_CONTROLLER->tx_data = c;
}

docs.title: Timer Driver
docs.text:
typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t ctrl;
    volatile uint32_t status;
    volatile uint32_t count;
    volatile uint32_t compare;
} timer_controller_t;

#define TIMER_CONTROLLER ((timer_controller_t*) TIMER_BASE)

void timer_init(uint32_t compare_value) {
    TIMER_CONTROLLER->compare = compare_value;
    TIMER_CONTROLLER->ctrl = 0x1;  // Enable timer
}

uint32_t timer_get_count(void) {
    return TIMER_CONTROLLER->count;
}

docs.title: GPIO Driver

typedef struct {

}

void gpio_set_outputs(uint32_t values) {

}

uint32_t gpio_get_inputs(void) {
    return GPIO_CONTROLLER->in;
}

docs.text: This document provides detailed information about the Memory Map API for the Open AXI Interconnect system. The memory map defines the address space layout and provides programmatic access to all peripherals and memory regions.

docs.title: Address Space Layout
docs.text:
The system implements a 32-bit address space organized into distinct regions:

Address Range           Size    Region
─────────────────────── ─────── ──────────────
0x0000_0000-0x0000_FFFF 64 KB   RAM Controller
0x4000_0000-0x4000_0FFF 4 KB    UART Controller
0x4001_0000-0x4001_0FFF 4 KB    Timer Module
0x4002_0000-0x4002_0FFF 4 KB    GPIO Controller
0x4003_0000-0xFFFF_FFFF ~4GB    Reserved

docs.title: Address Constants
docs.text:
Programmatic access to memory regions through defined constants:

#define RAM_BASE        0x00000000
#define UART_BASE       0x40000000
#define TIMER_BASE      0x40010000
#define GPIO_BASE       0x40020000

docs.title: Memory Region
docs.text:
• Base Address: 0x0000_0000
  • Size: 64 KB (0x10000)
  • End Address: 0x0000_FFFF

docs.title: Memory Array Access
docs.text: The RAM controller implements indirect memory access: - Write ADDRESS register (0x08) to set memory location - Write DATA register (0x0C) to store data at that location - Read DATA register (0x0C) to retrieve data from that location

    if (is_valid_address(test_address)) {
        printf("Address 0x%08X is valid\n", test_address);

docs.title: Register Access Pattern
docs.text:
void example_register_access() {
    // Get register information
    register_info_t reg_info = get_register_info(UART_BASE, 0x0000);
    printf("Register: %s, Access: %s\n", reg_info.name, reg_info.access_type);

    // Enumerate all UART registers
    register_list_t uart_regs = get_peripheral_registers(UART_BASE);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < uart_regs.count; i++) {
        printf("Register %s at offset 0x%04X\n", 
               uart_regs.registers[i].name, 
               uart_regs.registers[i].offset);
    }
}

    size_t peripheral_count;

    for (size_t i = 0; i < peripheral_count; i++) {

               peripherals[i].base_address,

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides comprehensive information about the Register API for the Open AXI Interconnect system. The Register API enables precise control and monitoring of all peripheral registers through standardized interfaces and data structures.

docs.title: Register Organization
docs.text: All peripherals implement a consistent register architecture: - 32-bit aligned register access - Standardized offset addressing - Defined access types (RW, RO, WO) - Predictable reset values - Bit-field level definitions

docs.title: Register Access Methods
docs.text: Two primary access methods are supported: 1. Direct Access: 32-bit register reads/writes 2. Bit-field Access: Individual bit or field manipulation

docs.title: Unified Register Interface
docs.text:
Standardized interface for all register access:

typedef enum {
    REG_ACCESS_RW,
    REG_ACCESS_RO,
    REG_ACCESS_WO
} register_access_type_t;

typedef struct {
    uint32_t offset;
    uint32_t size;
    register_access_type_t access_type;
    uint32_t reset_value;
    const char* name;
    const char* description;

docs.title: Basic Register Operations
docs.text:
#include "register_api.h"

void example_basic_operations() {
    // Enable RAM controller
    ram_control_enable();

    // Check if RAM is ready
    if (ram_status_is_ready()) {
        printf("RAM is ready\n");
    }

    // Write data to RAM
    ram_address_set(0x00000000);
    ram_data_write(0x12345678);

    // Read data from RAM
    uint32_t data = ram_data_read();
    printf("Read data: 0x%08X\n", data);
}

docs.text:
void example_uart_configuration() {
    // Enable UART with TX/RX
    uart_control_enable();
    uart_tx_enable();
    uart_rx_enable();

    // Wait for transmitter to be ready
    while (!uart_tx_is_ready()) {
        // Wait or yield
    }

    // Transmit character 'A'
    uart_tx_data_write('A');

    // Check for received data
    if (uart_rx_is_valid()) {
        uint8_t rx_data = uart_rx_data_read();
        printf("Received: %c\n", rx_data);
    }
}

docs.title: Timer Setup
docs.text:
void example_timer_setup() {
    // Set compare value for 1ms interrupt (assuming 100MHz clock)
    timer_compare_set(100000); // 100000 cycles = 1ms

    // Enable timer
    timer_enable();

    // Monitor counter
    uint32_t count = timer_count_get();
    printf("Timer count: %u\n", count);

    // Reset counter
    timer_reset();
}

docs.title: GPIO Configuration
docs.text:
void example_gpio_configuration() {
    // Configure GPIO 0-15 as output, 16-31 as input
    gpio_direction_set(0x0000FFFF);

    // Set output values for GPIO 0-15
    gpio_output_set(0x00005555);

    // Read all input values
    uint32_t inputs = gpio_input_get();
    printf("GPIO inputs: 0x%08X\n", inputs);

    // Set individual pin high
    gpio_pin_set_high(0); // Set GPIO 0 high
}

docs.title: Generic Register Access
docs.text:
void example_generic_access() {
    // Read UART control register using generic API
    uint32_t ctrl_value = register_read(UART_BASE, 0x00);
    printf("UART control: 0x%08X\n", ctrl_value);

    // Set a specific bit
    register_bit_set(UART_BASE, 0x00, 0); // Enable UART

    // Read a bit field
    uint32_t enable_bit = register_bit_get(UART_BASE, 0x00, 0);
    printf("UART enabled: %s\n", enable_bit ? "Yes" : "No");

    // Safe register access with error handling
    uint32_t value;
    register_error_t error = register_read_safe(0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00, &value);
    if (error != REGISTER_SUCCESS) {
        printf("Register read failed: %d\n", error);
    }
}

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect implements a lightweight, synthesizable AMBA AXI4-Lite based system-on-chip building block. It is intended for FPGA and ASIC designs that need a simple memory-mapped interconnect with a small set of peripherals.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
1. AXI4-Lite Interconnect - Single-master, multi-slave address decoder and router
  2. RAM Controller - 4KB memory array with control registers
  3. UART Controller - Minimal UART implementation
  4. Timer Module - Free-running counter with interrupt capability
  5. GPIO Controller - 32 bidirectional GPIO pins

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text: The design focuses on simplicity and synthesizability while maintaining compatibility with standard AXI4-Lite protocols. It's optimized for educational purposes and small-scale embedded systems where a full AXI4 implementation would be overkill.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Explore the individual sections to understand the detailed architecture of each component and how they interact within the system.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document details the implementation of the AXI4-Lite protocol in the Open AXI Interconnect system. Understanding the protocol implementation is essential for system integration and software development.

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Protocol Basics
docs.text: The ARM Advanced eXtensible Interface (AXI) protocol defines a high-performance, scalable interface for connecting IP blocks in System-on-Chip (SoC) designs. This implementation focuses on AXI4-Lite, a simplified subset optimized for memory-mapped I/O.

docs.title: Key Characteristics
docs.text:
• Separate Read and Write Channels: Independent address/data flows
  • No Burst Support: Single-beat transactions only
  • Fixed Response Types: OKAY and EXOKAY responses
  • No ID Signals: No transaction identification
  • No User Signals: No user-defined sideband signals

docs.title: Write Address Channel (AW)
docs.text: Signal Direction Description awaddr Input Write address awvalid Input Write address valid awready Output Write address ready

docs.title: Write Data Channel (W)
docs.text: Signal Direction Description wdata Input Write data wstrb Input Write strobe (byte enables) wvalid Input Write data valid wready Output Write data ready

docs.title: Write Response Channel (B)
docs.text: Signal Direction Description bresp Output Write response bvalid Output Write response valid bready Input Write response ready

docs.title: Read Address Channel (AR)
docs.text: Signal Direction Description araddr Input Read address arvalid Input Read address valid arready Output Read address ready

docs.title: Read Data Channel (R)
docs.text: Signal Direction Description rdata Output Read data rresp Output Read response rvalid Output Read data valid rready Input Read data ready

docs.title: Write Transaction
docs.text:
1. Address Phase:
  2. Master drives awaddr and asserts awvalid
  3. Slave asserts awready when ready to accept address

  4. Handshake completes when both awvalid and awready are asserted

  5. Data Phase:

  6. Master drives wdata, wstrb and asserts wvalid
  7. Slave asserts wready when ready to accept data

  8. Handshake completes when both wvalid and wready are asserted

  9. Response Phase:

  10. Slave drives bresp and asserts bvalid
  11. Master asserts bready when ready to accept response
  12. Handshake completes when both bvalid and bready are asserted

docs.title: Read Transaction
docs.text:
1. Address Phase:
  2. Master drives araddr and asserts arvalid
  3. Slave asserts arready when ready to accept address

  4. Handshake completes when both arvalid and arready are asserted

  5. Data Phase:

  6. Slave drives rdata, rresp and asserts rvalid
  7. Master asserts rready when ready to accept data
  8. Handshake completes when both rvalid and rready are asserted

docs.title: Write Responses (bresp)
docs.text: Value Name Description 0b00 OKAY Normal access success 0b01 EXOKAY Exclusive access success (not used in AXI4-Lite) 0b10 SLVERR Slave error 0b11 DECERR Decode error

docs.title: Read Responses (rresp)
docs.text: Same encoding as write responses.

docs.title: Address Decoding
docs.text: The interconnect implements fixed address decoding: - No runtime configuration - Combinational logic for address comparison - Priority-based slave selection

docs.title: Write Strobe Handling
docs.text: Byte-level write enables are supported through the wstrb signal: - wstrb[0] controls byte 0 (bits 7:0) - wstrb[1] controls byte 1 (bits 15:8) - wstrb[2] controls byte 2 (bits 23:16) - wstrb[3] controls byte 3 (bits 31:24)

docs.title: Backpressure Management
docs.text: Slaves can assert backpressure through ready signals: - awready for write address channel - wready for write data channel - arready for read address channel - rready for read data channel

docs.title: Setup and Hold Times
docs.text: All signals must meet standard setup and hold requirements: - Setup time relative to positive clock edge - Hold time relative to positive clock edge - Minimum pulse width for valid/ready signals

docs.title: Clock Domain Crossing
docs.text: All signals operate in a single clock domain: - Clock: clk - Reset: Active-low synchronous reset (rst_n)

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Compliance
docs.text: The implementation complies with AXI4-Lite requirements: - Single outstanding transaction per channel - No burst support (single beat only) - No exclusive access support - No cache/coherent attribute signals

docs.title: Restrictions
docs.text: Current implementation limitations: - Single master only - No pipelining of transactions - Fixed address map - No quality of service (QoS) support

docs.title: Decode Errors
docs.text: Addresses outside defined ranges: - Default to RAM controller (fallback behavior) - Return appropriate response codes - Log errors for debugging

docs.title: Protocol Violations
docs.text: Invalid signal sequences: - Misaligned valid/ready handshakes - Incorrect timing relationships - Unsupported signal combinations

docs.title: Latency
docs.text: Typical transaction latency: - Write: 3-4 clock cycles - Read: 3-4 clock cycles - Includes all handshake phases

docs.title: Throughput
docs.text: Maximum transaction rate: - Limited by single outstanding transaction - Dependent on slave response times - Clock frequency dependent

docs.title: Protocol Checking
docs.text: Implemented using SystemVerilog Assertions: - Valid/ready handshake checking - Signal integrity verification - Protocol sequence validation

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text: Coverage points include: - All valid transaction sequences - Backpressure scenarios - Error conditions - Boundary cases

docs.title: AXI4 Full Support
docs.text: Planned additions: - Burst transaction support - AXI ID signal implementation - Exclusive access support - Cache/coherent attribute handling

docs.title: Performance Improvements
docs.text: Potential optimizations: - Multiple outstanding transactions - Pipeline stage insertion - Reduced latency paths - Dynamic clock gating

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect implements a compliant subset of the AXI4-Lite protocol optimized for simplicity and reliability. The implementation provides predictable behavior suitable for embedded systems and educational purposes while maintaining compatibility with standard AXI tools and methodologies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document presents the Finite State Machine (FSM) diagrams for the Open AXI Interconnect system. Understanding these state machines is essential for comprehending the timing and behavior of each component.

docs.title: Write Transaction FSM
docs.text:
The AXI4-Lite write transaction follows a specific sequence of states:

IDLE ──AWVALID,WVALID──► HANDSHAKE ──AWREADY,WREADY──► RESPONSE ──BVALID──► IDLE
                           │                              │
                           │ BREADY                     │ BREADY
                           ▼                              ▼
                      WRITE_DATA ──────────────────► WAIT_BREADY

State Descriptions:

  1. IDLE: Waiting for write address and data valid signals
  2. HANDSHAKE: Address and data handshake in progress
  3. WRITE_DATA: Processing write data to peripheral
  4. RESPONSE: Generating write response
  5. WAIT_BREADY: Waiting for master to accept response

docs.title: Read Transaction FSM
docs.text:
The AXI4-Lite read transaction follows this state sequence:

IDLE ──ARVALID──► HANDSHAKE ──ARREADY──► PROCESS_READ ──RVALID──► IDLE
                     │                        │
                     │ RREADY               │ RREADY
                     ▼                        ▼
                WAIT_RREADY ───────────► WAIT_COMPLETE

State Descriptions:

  1. IDLE: Waiting for read address valid signal
  2. HANDSHAKE: Address handshake in progress
  3. PROCESS_READ: Retrieving data from peripheral
  4. WAIT_RREADY: Waiting for master to accept data
  5. WAIT_COMPLETE: Waiting for read completion

docs.title: RAM Controller States
docs.text:
The RAM controller implements a simple register-based FSM:

IDLE ──ACCESS──► PROCESS ──COMPLETE──► IDLE

States: - IDLE: Ready for new transactions - PROCESS: Handling register access or memory operation - COMPLETE: Transaction completion

docs.title: UART Controller States
docs.text:
IDLE ──WRITE──► STORE_DATA ──COMPLETE──► IDLE
  │
  └──READ──► RETRIEVE_DATA ──COMPLETE──► IDLE

States: - IDLE: Ready for transactions - STORE_DATA: Storing write data to registers - RETRIEVE_DATA: Retrieving read data from registers - COMPLETE: Transaction completion

docs.title: Timer Module States
docs.text:
The timer operates continuously but has FSM states for register access:

RUNNING ──REGISTER_ACCESS──► HANDLE_ACCESS ──COMPLETE──► RUNNING

States: - RUNNING: Continuous timer operation - HANDLE_ACCESS: Processing register read/write - COMPLETE: Access completion

docs.title: GPIO Controller States
docs.text:
IDLE ──REGISTER_ACCESS──► UPDATE_PINS ──COMPLETE──► IDLE

States: - IDLE: Ready for register access - UPDATE_PINS: Updating GPIO pin states - COMPLETE: Access completion

docs.title: Interconnect Routing FSM
docs.text:
The AXI interconnect uses combinational logic for routing rather than a traditional FSM, but the address decoding process can be visualized as:

ADDRESS_RECEIVE ──DECODE──► SELECT_SLAVE ──ROUTE_SIGNALS

Process Steps: 1. ADDRESS_RECEIVE: Capture incoming address 2. DECODE: Determine target slave based on address range 3. SELECT_SLAVE: Route signals to appropriate slave 4. ROUTE_SIGNALS: Forward transaction to selected slave

docs.title: Setup and Hold Times
docs.text: All FSM transitions observe standard setup and hold times: - Setup time: Minimum time before clock edge - Hold time: Minimum time after clock edge

docs.title: Clock Domain Considerations
docs.text: All FSMs operate in the same clock domain: - Single clock source: clk - Active edge: Positive edge - Reset: Synchronous active-low (rst_n)

docs.title: State Encoding
docs.text: States are typically encoded as: - Binary encoding for area efficiency - One-hot encoding for speed (used selectively) - Gray code for low power applications

docs.title: Reset Behavior
docs.text: All FSMs implement synchronous reset: - Reset occurs on negedge of rst_n - All states transition to defined reset state - Reset recovery time observed

docs.title: Glitch Prevention
docs.text: FSM implementations include: - Registered outputs to prevent glitches - Proper synchronization of asynchronous inputs - Metastability protection where needed

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Each FSM has been verified through cocotb simulations: - State transition coverage >95% - Timing constraint validation - Reset sequence verification - Error condition handling

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text: Planned improvements to FSM designs: - Power gating for low-power states - Dynamic frequency scaling support - Advanced error recovery mechanisms - Formal verification of state properties

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect implements deterministic FSMs that ensure predictable behavior under all operating conditions. The simplicity of these state machines contributes to the overall reliability and ease of verification of the system.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document defines the complete memory map for the Open AXI Interconnect system. Understanding the memory map is crucial for software development and system integration.

docs.title: Address Space Layout
docs.text:
The system utilizes a 32-bit address space organized into distinct regions for each peripheral. The memory map is fixed at compile time to minimize hardware complexity.

Address Range           Size    Peripheral
─────────────────────── ─────── ──────────────
0x0000_0000-0x0000_FFFF 64 KB   RAM Controller
0x4000_0000-0x4000_0FFF 4 KB    UART Controller
0x4001_0000-0x4001_0FFF 4 KB    Timer Module
0x4002_0000-0x4002_0FFF 4 KB    GPIO Controller
...                     ...     (Reserved)
──────────────────────────────────────────────
Total Addressable Space: ~4 GB

docs.title: RAM Controller (0x0000_0000)
docs.text: The RAM controller occupies the bottom 64KB of the address space.

docs.title: Address Range
docs.text:
• Base: 0x0000_0000
  • End: 0x0000_FFFF
  • Size: 64 KB (1024 × 32-bit words)

docs.title: Memory Organization
docs.text: The RAM controller implements a dual-access mechanism: 1. Control Registers (0x0000_0000 - 0x0000_000F) 2. Memory Array (accessed via address/data registers)

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: Addresses within the RAM region that are not control registers are handled by the address/data register mechanism: - Write to ADDRESS register (0x08) to set memory location - Write to DATA register (0x0C) to store data at that location - Read from DATA register (0x0C) to retrieve data from that location

docs.title: UART Controller (0x4000_0000)
docs.text: The UART controller provides serial communication capabilities.

docs.title: Address Range
docs.text:
• Base: 0x4000_0000
  • End: 0x4000_0FFF
  • Size: 4 KB

docs.title: Address Decoding
docs.text:
All addresses within this range route to the UART peripheral. The specific register is determined by the lower 4 bits of the address:

Address Offset Register Function 0x0000_0000 CTRL Control register 0x0000_0004 STATUS Status register 0x0000_0008 TX_DATA Transmit data 0x0000_000C RX_DATA Receive data

docs.title: Timer Module (0x4001_0000)
docs.text: The timer module provides timing and interrupt capabilities.

docs.title: Address Range
docs.text:
• Base: 0x4001_0000
  • End: 0x4001_0FFF
  • Size: 4 KB

docs.title: Address Decoding
docs.text:
Similar to UART, addresses within this range route to timer registers:

Address Offset Register Function 0x0000_0000 CTRL Control register 0x0000_0004 STATUS Status register 0x0000_0008 COUNT Current counter value 0x0000_000C COMPARE Interrupt compare value

docs.title: GPIO Controller (0x4002_0000)
docs.text: The GPIO controller manages 32 bidirectional I/O pins.

docs.title: Address Range
docs.text:
• Base: 0x4002_0000
  • End: 0x4002_0FFF
  • Size: 4 KB

docs.title: Address Decoding
docs.text:
GPIO registers are accessed via the following offsets:

Address Offset Register Function 0x0000_0000 DIR Direction control 0x0000_0004 OUT Output value 0x0000_0008 IN Input value (read-only)

docs.title: Address Decoding Logic
docs.text:
The interconnect uses a simple priority-based address decoder:

  1. Addresses 0x0000_0000 to 0x0000_FFFF → RAM Controller
  2. Addresses 0x4000_0000 to 0x4000_0FFF → UART Controller
  3. Addresses 0x4001_0000 to 0x4001_0FFF → Timer Module
  4. Addresses 0x4002_0000 to 0x4002_0FFF → GPIO Controller
  5. All other addresses → Default to RAM (fallback)

Address: 0x4000_0000
Data:    0x0000_0007  // Enable UART, TX, RX

docs.title: Read Timer Counter Value
docs.text:
Address: 0x4001_0008
Response: Current 32-bit counter value

docs.title: Write GPIO Output Values
docs.text:
Address: 0x4002_0004
Data:    0xA5A5_A5A5  // Set GPIO output pins

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect is designed as a lightweight, synthesizable System-on-Chip (SoC) building block that implements a subset of the AMBA AXI4-Lite protocol. This document provides a comprehensive overview of the system architecture, design principles, and implementation details.

docs.title: 1. AXI4-Lite Interconnect
docs.text:
The central component that routes transactions between the master and multiple slave peripherals. Key features include:

  • Single master, multi-slave topology
  • Fixed address decoding scheme
  • No pipelining or outstanding transactions
  • AXI4-Lite protocol compliance (no burst support)

docs.title: 2. RAM Controller
docs.text:
Implements a simple memory array with associated control registers:

  • 4KB memory array (1024 × 32-bit words)
  • Control register for enabling/disabling
  • Status register indicating readiness
  • Address register for memory access
  • Data register for read/write operations

docs.title: 3. UART Controller
docs.text:
Minimal UART implementation providing basic serial communication:

  • Control register for enabling transmitter/receiver
  • Status register indicating transmission readiness
  • TX data register for outgoing characters
  • RX data register for incoming characters

docs.title: 4. Timer Module
docs.text:
Free-running counter with interrupt generation capability:

  • 32-bit free-running counter
  • Configurable compare value for interrupt generation
  • Control register for enabling/resetting
  • Status register indicating activity
  • Interrupt output signal

docs.title: 5. GPIO Controller
docs.text:
32 bidirectional GPIO pins with flexible configuration:

  • Direction register (input/output control)
  • Output value register
  • Input value register (read-only)

docs.title: Address Map
docs.text:
The system uses a 32-bit address space with the following memory map:

Peripheral Base Address End Address Size RAM 0x0000_0000 0x0000_FFFF 64 KB UART 0x4000_0000 0x4000_0FFF 4 KB Timer 0x4001_0000 0x4001_0FFF 4 KB GPIO 0x4002_0000 0x4002_0FFF 4 KB

docs.title: Protocol Limitations
docs.text:
Version 1 of the system implements only AXI4-Lite features:

  • Single beat reads/writes only (no bursts)
  • No AXI IDs
  • No cache/coherent attributes
  • 32-bit data width

docs.title: Implementation Choices
docs.text:
The design makes several intentional trade-offs:

  1. Single Master: Simplifies arbitration logic
  2. No Pipelining: Reduces complexity and resource usage
  3. Fixed Address Map: Eliminates runtime configuration overhead
  4. Minimal Peripherals: Focuses on core functionality

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Planned improvements include:

  • AXI4 full protocol support
  • Multi-master capability
  • Burst transaction support
  • Additional peripheral controllers
  • DMA controller
  • Interrupt controller

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect provides a solid foundation for learning about AXI protocols and implementing simple embedded systems. Its modular design allows easy extension with additional peripherals while maintaining predictable behavior and resource usage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides a complete specification of all registers in the Open AXI Interconnect system. Each register is described with its address offset, access type, reset value, and bit field definitions.

docs.title: Register Conventions
docs.text:
All registers follow these conventions:

  • Width: 32 bits
  • Access Size: 32-bit aligned access only
  • Address Alignment: 4-byte boundaries
  • Access Types:
  • RW: Readable and writable
  • RO: Read-only
  • WO: Write-only (write value ignored for reads)

docs.title: RAM Controller Registers
docs.text: Base Address: 0x0000_0000

docs.title: Control Register (Offset: 0x00)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:1 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 0 ENABLE RW 0 RAM enable bit

docs.title: Status Register (Offset: 0x04)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:1 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 0 READY RO 1 RAM ready indicator

docs.title: Address Register (Offset: 0x08)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 ADDR RW 0x0000_0000 Memory address pointer

docs.title: Data Register (Offset: 0x0C)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 DATA RW 0x0000_0000 Read/write data at address

docs.title: UART Controller Registers
docs.text: Base Address: 0x4000_0000

docs.title: Control Register (Offset: 0x00)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:3 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 2 RX_ENABLE RW 0 Enable receiver 1 TX_ENABLE RW 0 Enable transmitter 0 ENABLE RW 0 Enable UART

docs.title: Status Register (Offset: 0x04)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:2 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 1 RX_VALID RO 0 Received data available 0 TX_READY RO 1 Transmit available

docs.title: TX Data Register (Offset: 0x08)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:8 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 7:0 TX_BYTE WO 0x00 Transmit data byte

docs.title: RX Data Register (Offset: 0x0C)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:8 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 7:0 RX_BYTE RO 0x00 Received data byte

docs.title: Timer Module Registers
docs.text: Base Address: 0x4001_0000

docs.title: Control Register (Offset: 0x00)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:2 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 1 RESET RW 0 Reset counter to zero 0 ENABLE RW 0 Enable counting

docs.title: Status Register (Offset: 0x04)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:1 - - 0x0000_0000 Reserved 0 ACTIVE RO 0 Timer is enabled

docs.title: Count Register (Offset: 0x08)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 COUNT RO 0x0000_0000 Current counter value

docs.title: Compare Register (Offset: 0x0C)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 COMPARE RW 0x0000_0000 Interrupt compare value

docs.title: GPIO Controller Registers
docs.text: Base Address: 0x4002_0000

docs.title: Direction Register (Offset: 0x00)
docs.text:
Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 DIR RW 0x0000_0000 Pin direction (1=output, 0=input)

Bit mapping: - Bit 0: GPIO[0] direction - Bit 1: GPIO[1] direction - ... - Bit 31: GPIO[31] direction

docs.title: Output Register (Offset: 0x04)
docs.text:
Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 OUT RW 0x0000_0000 Output pin values

Bit mapping: - Bit 0: GPIO[0] output value - Bit 1: GPIO[1] output value - ... - Bit 31: GPIO[31] output value

docs.title: Input Register (Offset: 0x08)
docs.text:
Bits Name Access Reset Description 31:0 IN RO 0x0000_0000 Input pin values

Bit mapping: - Bit 0: GPIO[0] input value - Bit 1: GPIO[1] input value - ... - Bit 31: GPIO[31] input value

docs.title: Access Timing
docs.text: All register accesses follow the AXI4-Lite protocol timing:

docs.title: Write Transaction
docs.text:
1. Master asserts AWVALID with address
  2. Master asserts WVALID with data and write strobe
  3. Slave asserts AWREADY and WREADY
  4. Slave asserts BVALID with response
  5. Master asserts BREADY

docs.title: Read Transaction
docs.text:
1. Master asserts ARVALID with address
  2. Slave asserts ARREADY
  3. Slave asserts RVALID with data and response
  4. Master asserts RREADY

docs.title: Reset Behavior
docs.text: Upon reset deassertion: 1. All registers initialize to their specified reset values 2. Timers start counting if enabled 3. UART transmitter becomes ready 4. GPIO pins assume default states based on direction settings

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The system handles invalid accesses as follows: - Out-of-range addresses: Default to RAM controller - Unaligned accesses: Not supported (32-bit aligned only) - Invalid register accesses: Return zero for reads, ignore writes

docs.title: Initialize UART
docs.text:
// Enable UART with TX/RX
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40000000) = 0x7;

// Check if transmitter ready
while(!(*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40000004) & 0x1));

// Transmit character 'A'
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40000008) = 0x41;

docs.title: Configure Timer
docs.text:
// Set compare value for 1ms interrupt
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x4001000C) = 0x2710; // 10000 cycles

// Enable timer
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40010000) = 0x1;

// Poll for interrupt or use timer_irq signal

docs.title: Configure GPIO
docs.text:
// Set GPIO 0-15 as output, 16-31 as input
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40020000) = 0x0000FFFF;

// Set output values for GPIO 0-15
*((volatile uint32_t*)0x40020004) = 0x00005555;

// Read input values from GPIO 16-31
uint32_t inputs = *((volatile uint32_t*)0x40020008);

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Each register has been verified through cocotb test cases: - test_axi_lite_basic validates RAM controller registers - test_uart validates UART controller registers - test_timer validates Timer module registers - test_gpio validates GPIO controller registers

All tests pass, confirming correct register behavior and address decoding.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect is a synthesizable, open-source AXI4/AXI4-Lite crossbar interconnect written in SystemVerilog. It provides a complete system-on-chip building block with essential peripherals for embedded applications.

  6. Begin developing your own applications

docs.text: Before beginning, ensure your system meets these minimum requirements:

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The Open AXI Interconnect implements a single-master, multi-slave architecture:

AXI Master
    ↓
AXI Interconnect
    ↓
├── RAM Controller (64KB)
├── UART Controller
├── Timer Module
└── GPIO Controller (32 pins)

docs.text:
Understanding the memory map is crucial for system usage:

Peripheral Base Address Size RAM 0x0000_0000 64KB UART 0x4000_0000 4KB Timer 0x4001_0000 4KB GPIO 0x4002_0000 4KB

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The axi_lite_interconnect module implements a single-master, multi-slave AXI4-Lite crossbar interconnect. It provides address decoding and routing functionality to connect a master to multiple slave peripherals.

docs.title: Module Declaration
docs.text:
module axi_lite_interconnect #(
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 32,
    parameter NUM_SLAVES = 4
)(
    // Master side (only one master supported in this version)
    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   m_awaddr,
    input  logic                    m_awvalid,
    output logic                    m_awready,

    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   m_wdata,
    input  logic [(DATA_WIDTH/8)-1:0] m_wstrb,
    input  logic                    m_wvalid,
    output logic                    m_wready,

    output logic [1:0]              m_bresp,
    output logic                    m_bvalid,
    input  logic                    m_bready,

    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   m_araddr,
    input  logic                    m_arvalid,
    output logic                    m_arready,

    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   m_rdata,
    output logic [1:0]              m_rresp,
    output logic                    m_rvalid,
    input  logic                    m_rready,

    // Slave side
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] s_awaddr,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_awvalid,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_awready,

    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][DATA_WIDTH-1:0] s_wdata,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][(DATA_WIDTH/8)-1:0] s_wstrb,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_wvalid,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_wready,

    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][1:0]           s_bresp,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_bvalid,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_bready,

    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] s_araddr,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_arvalid,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_arready,

    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][DATA_WIDTH-1:0] s_rdata,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0][1:0]           s_rresp,
    input  logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_rvalid,
    output logic [NUM_SLAVES-1:0]                s_rready
);

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description ADDR_WIDTH 32 Width of address bus in bits DATA_WIDTH 32 Width of data bus in bits NUM_SLAVES 4 Number of slave interfaces

docs.title: Master Side (Single Master Interface)
docs.text:
Write address channel: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | m_awaddr | Input | Master write address | | m_awvalid | Input | Master write address valid | | m_awready | Output | Master write address ready |

Write data channel: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | m_wdata | Input | Master write data | | m_wstrb | Input | Master write strobe | | m_wvalid | Input | Master write data valid | | m_wready | Output | Master write data ready |

Write response channel: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | m_bresp | Output | Master write response | | m_bvalid | Output | Master write response valid | | m_bready | Input | Master write response ready |

Read address channel: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | m_araddr | Input | Master read address | | m_arvalid | Input | Master read address valid | | m_arready | Output | Master read address ready |

Read data channel: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | m_rdata | Output | Master read data | | m_rresp | Output | Master read response | | m_rvalid | Output | Master read data valid | | m_rready | Input | Master read data ready |

docs.title: Slave Side (Multiple Slave Interfaces)
docs.text: Arrays of slave interfaces, indexed by slave number: | Port | Direction | Description | |------|-----------|-------------| | s_awaddr | Output | Slave write addresses | | s_awvalid | Output | Slave write address valid signals | | s_awready | Input | Slave write address ready signals | | s_wdata | Output | Slave write data | | s_wstrb | Output | Slave write strobes | | s_wvalid | Output | Slave write data valid signals | | s_wready | Input | Slave write data ready signals | | s_bresp | Input | Slave write responses | | s_bvalid | Input | Slave write response valid signals | | s_bready | Output | Slave write response ready signals | | s_araddr | Output | Slave read addresses | | s_arvalid | Output | Slave read address valid signals | | s_arready | Input | Slave read address ready signals | | s_rdata | Input | Slave read data | | s_rresp | Input | Slave read responses | | s_rvalid | Input | Slave read data valid signals | | s_rready | Output | Slave read data ready signals |

docs.title: Type Definitions
docs.text:
typedef enum logic [1:0] {
    SLAVE_RAM   = 2'd0,
    SLAVE_UART  = 2'd1,
    SLAVE_TIMER = 2'd2,
    SLAVE_GPIO  = 2'd3
} slave_sel_t;

Enumeration defining the slave selection indices.

docs.title: Signal Declarations
docs.text: Signal Type Description write_sel slave_sel_t Selected slave for write transaction read_sel slave_sel_t Selected slave for read transaction

docs.title: Address Map Constants
docs.text: Fixed address ranges for slave selection: - RAM: 0x0000_0000 to 0x0000_FFFF - UART: 0x4000_0000 to 0x4000_0FFF - Timer: 0x4001_0000 to 0x4001_0FFF - GPIO: 0x4002_0000 to 0x4002_0FFF

docs.title: Address Decoding
docs.text:
The address decoding function determines which slave should handle a transaction:

function automatic slave_sel_t decode(input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] addr);
    begin
        if      ((addr >= UART_BASE)  && (addr <= UART_END))  decode = SLAVE_UART;
        else if ((addr >= TIMER_BASE) && (addr <= TIMER_END)) decode = SLAVE_TIMER;
        else if ((addr >= GPIO_BASE)  && (addr <= GPIO_END))  decode = SLAVE_GPIO;
        else                                                   decode = SLAVE_RAM;
    end
endfunction

docs.title: Write Routing Logic
docs.text:
The write routing logic connects master signals to the appropriate slave:

always_comb begin
    // Broadcast addresses and data to all slaves
    s_awaddr  = {NUM_SLAVES{m_awaddr}};
    s_awvalid = {NUM_SLAVES{1'b0}};
    s_wdata   = {NUM_SLAVES{m_wdata}};
    s_wstrb   = {NUM_SLAVES{m_wstrb}};
    s_wvalid  = {NUM_SLAVES{1'b0}};
    s_bready  = {NUM_SLAVES{1'b0}};

    // Activate only the selected slave
    s_awvalid[write_sel] = m_awvalid;
    s_wvalid [write_sel] = m_wvalid;
    s_bready [write_sel] = m_bready;

    // Connect master responses from selected slave
    m_awready = s_awready[write_sel];
    m_wready  = s_wready [write_sel];
    m_bresp   = s_bresp  [write_sel];
    m_bvalid  = s_bvalid [write_sel];
end

docs.title: Read Routing Logic
docs.text:
Similar logic handles read transactions:

always_comb begin
    // Broadcast addresses to all slaves
    s_araddr  = {NUM_SLAVES{m_araddr}};
    s_arvalid = {NUM_SLAVES{1'b0}};
    s_rready  = {NUM_SLAVES{1'b0}};

    // Activate only the selected slave
    s_arvalid[read_sel] = m_arvalid;
    s_rready [read_sel] = m_rready;

    // Connect master responses from selected slave
    m_arready = s_arready[read_sel];
    m_rdata   = s_rdata  [read_sel];
    m_rresp   = s_rresp  [read_sel];
    m_rvalid  = s_rvalid [read_sel];
end

docs.title: Single Master Support
docs.text: The interconnect supports only one master, simplifying the design: - No arbitration logic required - Deterministic routing behavior - Reduced resource utilization

docs.title: Fixed Address Mapping
docs.text: Address decoding uses fixed ranges: - No runtime configuration - Combinational logic implementation - Predictable performance characteristics

docs.title: Full AXI4-Lite Compliance
docs.text: Implements all required AXI4-Lite channels: - Write address, write data, write response - Read address, read data - Proper handshake signaling

docs.title: Latency
docs.text: Transaction latency is minimal: - Address decoding: Combinational logic (single cycle) - Signal routing: Direct connection (single cycle) - Total interconnect overhead: 1-2 cycles

docs.title: Resource Utilization
docs.text: Resource usage scales linearly with number of slaves: - Address decoding logic: Fixed (independent of slaves) - Routing multiplexers: Proportional to NUM_SLAVES - No FIFOs or buffering (no outstanding transactions)

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The interconnect has been verified through: - Functional simulation with cocotb testbenches - Assertion-based protocol checking - Address decoding verification - Routing correctness validation

docs.title: Integration
docs.text: To integrate the interconnect: 1. Connect master interface to your AXI master 2. Connect slave interfaces to your peripherals 3. Ensure consistent ADDR_WIDTH and DATA_WIDTH parameters 4. Verify address map matches peripheral expectations

docs.title: Parameter Selection
docs.text: Recommended parameter values: - ADDR_WIDTH: 32 bits (standard for most systems) - DATA_WIDTH: 32 bits (can be adjusted for wider data paths) - NUM_SLAVES: Match to actual number of peripherals

docs.title: Address Map Modification
docs.text: To modify the address map: 1. Update the address constants in the module 2. Adjust the decode function logic 3. Ensure consistency with peripheral address expectations 4. Update documentation to reflect changes

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: Current implementation limitations: - Single master only (no multi-master support) - No pipelining or outstanding transactions - Fixed address map (requires RTL modification) - No quality of service (QoS) support - No protection or region signaling

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text: Planned improvements: - Multi-master support with arbitration - Outstanding transaction support - Configurable address mapping - QoS and protection features - Performance monitoring capabilities

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The axi_lite_interconnect module provides a simple, efficient solution for connecting a single AXI4-Lite master to multiple slave peripherals. Its fixed address mapping and single-master design make it ideal for embedded systems where simplicity and predictability are valued over maximum flexibility.

docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CONTROL RW RAM enable control 0x04 STATUS RO RAM status indicators 0x08 ADDRESS RW Memory address pointer 0x0C DATA RW Memory data access

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: The RAM controller implements a dual-access mechanism: 1. Direct register access for control/status 2. Indirect memory access via address/data registers

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
// Write data to memory location 0
axi_write(RAM_BASE + 0x08, 32'h00000000); // Set address
axi_write(RAM_BASE + 0x0C, 32'h12345678); // Write data

// Read data from memory location 0
axi_read(RAM_BASE + 0x08); // Set address
data = axi_read(RAM_BASE + 0x0C); // Read data

docs.title: Module: uart
docs.text: The UART controller provides basic serial communication capabilities.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Control register for enabling transmitter/receiver
  • Status register indicating transmission readiness
  • TX data register for outgoing characters
  • RX data register for incoming characters

docs.title: Address Offsets
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CTRL RW UART control settings 0x04 STATUS RO UART status indicators 0x08 TX_DATA WO Transmit data register 0x0C RX_DATA RO Receive data register

docs.title: Control Register (CTRL)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Description 31:3 - - Reserved 2 RX_ENABLE RW Enable receiver 1 TX_ENABLE RW Enable transmitter 0 ENABLE RW Enable UART

docs.title: Status Register (STATUS)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Description 31:2 - - Reserved 1 RX_VALID RO Received data available 0 TX_READY RO Transmit available

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: The current implementation provides a minimal UART model: - No actual serial transmission/reception - Data capture for TX register - Placeholder for RX functionality - Always-ready status for simplicity

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
// Enable UART with TX/RX
axi_write(UART_BASE + 0x00, 32'h00000007);

// Transmit character 'A'
axi_write(UART_BASE + 0x08, 32'h00000041);

// Check if transmitter ready
status = axi_read(UART_BASE + 0x04);
if (status & 1) {
    // Transmitter ready
}

docs.title: Module: timer
docs.text: The timer module provides timing capabilities with interrupt generation.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Free-running 32-bit counter
  • Configurable compare value for interrupt generation
  • Control register for enabling/resetting
  • Status register indicating activity
  • Interrupt output signal

docs.title: Address Offsets
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CTRL RW Timer control settings 0x04 STATUS RO Timer status indicators 0x08 COUNT RO Current counter value 0x0C COMPARE RW Interrupt compare value

docs.title: Control Register (CTRL)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Description 31:2 - - Reserved 1 RESET RW Reset counter to zero 0 ENABLE RW Enable counting

docs.title: Status Register (STATUS)
docs.text: Bits Name Access Description 31:1 - - Reserved 0 ACTIVE RO Timer is enabled

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: The timer implements a free-running counter: - Increments every clock cycle when enabled - Generates interrupt when count >= compare value - Reset functionality to clear counter - Continuous operation regardless of AXI transactions

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
// Set compare value for interrupt
axi_write(TIMER_BASE + 0x0C, 32'h00002710); // 10000 cycles

// Enable timer
axi_write(TIMER_BASE + 0x00, 32'h00000001);

// Read current count
count = axi_read(TIMER_BASE + 0x08);

// Check interrupt status
// timer_irq signal will be high when count >= compare

docs.title: Module: gpio
docs.text: The GPIO controller manages 32 bidirectional I/O pins.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 32 bidirectional GPIO pins
  • Direction register (input/output control)
  • Output value register
  • Input value register (read-only)

docs.title: Address Offsets
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 DIR RW Pin direction control 0x04 OUT RW Output pin values 0x08 IN RO Input pin values

docs.title: Direction Register (DIR)
docs.text: Each bit controls the direction of the corresponding GPIO pin: - 0: Input (high-impedance) - 1: Output (driven)

docs.title: Output Register (OUT)
docs.text: Each bit sets the output value for pins configured as outputs.

docs.title: Input Register (IN)
docs.text: Each bit reflects the current input value for all pins.

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: The GPIO controller provides: - Bidirectional pin control - Individual pin direction configuration - Simultaneous read/write of all 32 pins - External pin connections via inout port

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
// Configure GPIO 0-15 as output, 16-31 as input
axi_write(GPIO_BASE + 0x00, 32'h0000FFFF);

// Set output values for GPIO 0-15
axi_write(GPIO_BASE + 0x04, 32'h00005555);

// Read input values from all pins
inputs = axi_read(GPIO_BASE + 0x08);

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Slave Interface
docs.text: All peripherals implement the same AXI4-Lite slave interface pattern: - Combinational ready signal assignment for immediate response - Registered valid signal generation for response timing - Byte-level write strobe handling through helper function - Address-based register selection

docs.title: Register Access Helper
docs.text:
Common helper function for byte-level write operations: 

function automatic [31:0] apply_wstrb(
    input [31:0] old_val,
    input [31:0] new_val,
    input [3:0]  strb
);
    reg [31:0] mask;
    begin
        mask = {{8{strb[3]}}, {8{strb[2]}}, {8{strb[1]}}, {8{strb[0]}}};
        apply_wstrb = (old_val & ~mask) | (new_val & mask);
    end
endfunction

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The axi_subsystem module serves as the top-level integration point for the Open AXI Interconnect system. It instantiates all peripheral controllers and the AXI interconnect, providing a single AXI4-Lite master interface for external connectivity.

docs.title: Module Declaration
docs.text:
module axi_subsystem #(
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 32
)(
    input  logic                    clk,
    input  logic                    rst_n,

    // AXI4-Lite master interface
    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   awaddr,
    input  logic                    awvalid,
    output logic                    awready,

    input  logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   wdata,
    input  logic [(DATA_WIDTH/8)-1:0] wstrb,
    input  logic                    wvalid,
    output logic                    wready,

    output logic [1:0]              bresp,
    output logic                    bvalid,
    input  logic                    bready,

    input  logic [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0]   araddr,
    input  logic                    arvalid,
    output logic                    arready,

    output logic [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]   rdata,
    output logic [1:0]              rresp,
    output logic                    rvalid,
    input  logic                    rready,

    // External peripheral signals
    output logic                    uart_tx,
    input  logic                    uart_rx,
    output logic                    timer_irq,
    inout  logic [31:0]             gpio_pins
);

docs.text: Parameter Default Description ADDR_WIDTH 32 Width of address bus in bits DATA_WIDTH 32 Width of data bus in bits

assert_<name>: assert property (
    <antecedent> |-> <consequent>
) else begin
    $error("<message>");
end

// Valid signal stability
valid_stable: assert property (
    ($rose(valid) && !ready) |=> $stable(valid)
) else begin
    $error("Valid signal unstable during handshake");
end

    $past(valid_state) && $changed(state) |->
    legal_transition($past(state), state)
) else begin

end

docs.title: TC001: RAM Controller Basic Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate RAM controller register access and basic memory operations Steps: 1. Write to RAM control register 2. Read back control register value 3. Write to RAM address register 4. Write data to RAM data register 5. Read back data from RAM data register Expected Results: All reads return expected values

docs.title: TC002: UART Controller Basic Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate UART controller register access Steps: 1. Write to UART control register 2. Read back control register value 3. Write to UART TX data register 4. Read back TX data register value 5. Read UART status register Expected Results: Control and data registers accessible, status reflects correct state

docs.title: TC003: Timer Module Basic Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate timer module register access Steps: 1. Write to timer compare register 2. Write to timer control register 3. Read back control register value 4. Read timer count register after delay 5. Check timer interrupt signal Expected Results: Registers accessible, counter increments, interrupt asserts

docs.title: TC004: GPIO Controller Basic Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate GPIO controller register access Steps: 1. Write to GPIO direction register 2. Read back direction register value 3. Write to GPIO output register 4. Read back output register value 5. Read GPIO input register Expected Results: All registers accessible, input reflects output for configured pins

docs.title: TC005: Memory Array Operations
docs.text: Objective: Validate RAM memory array read/write operations Steps: 1. Write data to multiple memory locations 2. Read back data from each location 3. Perform sequential read/write operations 4. Verify data integrity across operations Expected Results: Data integrity maintained, no corruption

docs.title: TC006: UART Transmission Sequence
docs.text: Objective: Validate complete UART transmission sequence Steps: 1. Enable UART controller 2. Configure UART for transmission 3. Write multiple data bytes to TX register 4. Monitor status for transmission completion 5. Verify interrupt behavior if applicable Expected Results: Transmission sequence successful, status accurate

docs.title: TC007: Timer Interrupt Generation
docs.text: Objective: Validate timer interrupt generation and handling Steps: 1. Configure timer compare value 2. Enable timer counting 3. Monitor counter progression 4. Verify interrupt assertion at compare value 5. Test interrupt clearing mechanism Expected Results: Interrupt correctly asserts at compare value

docs.title: TC008: GPIO Pin Configuration
docs.text: Objective: Validate comprehensive GPIO pin configuration Steps: 1. Configure various pin directions 2. Set output values for output pins 3. Read input values for input pins 4. Change pin directions dynamically 5. Verify input/output behavior consistency Expected Results: Correct behavior for all pin configurations

docs.title: TC009: Rapid Transaction Sequences
docs.text: Objective: Validate system behavior under rapid transaction sequences Steps: 1. Execute continuous write transactions to different peripherals 2. Mix read and write transactions rapidly 3. Monitor system response times 4. Check for transaction conflicts or losses Expected Results: System maintains integrity under stress

docs.title: TC010: Boundary Address Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate behavior at memory map boundaries Steps: 1. Access addresses at peripheral boundaries 2. Access addresses at memory array boundaries 3. Access addresses beyond defined ranges 4. Verify appropriate error handling Expected Results: Correct handling of boundary conditions

docs.title: TC011: Reset Recovery
docs.text: Objective: Validate system recovery from reset conditions Steps: 1. Execute normal transactions 2. Assert system reset 3. Deassert reset after appropriate delay 4. Resume normal transactions 5. Verify register initialization Expected Results: Proper reset behavior, correct initialization

docs.title: TC012: Invalid Register Access
docs.text: Objective: Validate system behavior with invalid register accesses Steps: 1. Attempt to access undefined register offsets 2. Attempt to write to read-only registers 3. Attempt to read from write-only registers 4. Verify appropriate error responses Expected Results: Graceful handling of invalid accesses

docs.title: TC013: Protocol Violation Scenarios
docs.text: Objective: Validate system resilience to protocol violations Steps: 1. Assert multiple valid signals simultaneously incorrectly 2. Violate timing relationships between signals 3. Send malformed address/data values 4. Verify system error handling Expected Results: System maintains stability, handles violations gracefully
